Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.core
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.language

Class MessageText

java.lang.Object
io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.language.MessageText
public final class MessageText extends Object
Shortens and escapes text a language didn't write, such as a fact name, an option value, an import or its library's own error text, for a message, as the engine does in its own messages. Such text can hold line breaks, bidi controls or lone surrogates, and a message the engine or a language logs mustn't let it start a log line of its own or hide part of the line. It delegates to the engine's own escaping rather than keeping a copy of it.

Use it for text the engine shows as it came: a message a language logs itself, the message of an exception its own library sees first, and the issues it throws in an InvalidExpressionException, which the engine copies untouched into the RuleCompilationException it reports. Use quote(java.lang.String) for a name and escape(truncate(text)) for other text.

The engine shortens to 1,000 characters and escapes the message of an InvalidExpressionException, the message of a warning's issue when it logs it, and the message of an exception from ExpressionCompiler.checkFactName(java.lang.String) when it logs it or, at load(), reports it for a declared fact. Leave a message the engine shortens raw: the engine escapes it itself, and shortening escaped text can cut an escape in half. The count of what was left out would then count escaped characters too. The MVEL language escapes the messages of its compile errors, and of its rejections of a fact name, an option's name or value, a declared or output type, or any language imports, itself, but fits each escaped message in 1,000 characters, so the engine never shortens one it reports directly.

The escapes, the note ... (N more characters) and the limits of 200 characters (UTF-16 units) for a name and 1,000 for other text are fixed for 2.x. Which characters are escaped follows Unicode: format characters are read from the running JDK's Unicode version, so a later JDK, or a later 2.x release, may escape more characters as Unicode marks them.

  • Method Details

    • escape

      public static String escape(String text)
      Escapes text for a message, without shortening it. \n, \r and \t become those two-character escapes. Every other ISO control character, line or paragraph separator, format character (category Cf), other Default_Ignorable_Code_Point character and lone surrogate becomes a backslash, u and four lowercase hex digits, one for each UTF-16 unit, so an escaped character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane becomes two escapes, and each escaped unit shows as 2 or 6 characters. Everything else is kept, a valid surrogate pair such as an emoji included. A backslash isn't escaped, so escaping text twice gives the same text.

      Format characters are those of the running JDK's Unicode version (Character.getType(int)). The other default-ignorable characters are U+034F, U+115F to U+1160, U+17B4 to U+17B5, U+180B to U+180F, U+2065, U+3164, U+FE00 to U+FE0F, U+FFA0, U+FFF0 to U+FFF8 and U+E0000 to U+E0FFF.

      To put long text in a message, shorten it first and escape it after, escape(truncate(text)), as the engine does, so a cut never falls inside an escape. The result can be up to six times longer than the 1,000 characters kept, since a character escapes to at most 6, so use it only for text the engine won't shorten again. Leave a message the engine shortens raw: the engine escapes it itself, and shortening escaped text can cut an escape in half (see the class description).

      Parameters:
      text - The text
      Returns:
      The text, escaped
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if text is null

    • truncate

      public static String truncate(String text)
      Shortens text for a message to at most 1,000 characters (UTF-16 units), without escaping it. Text of at most 1,000 characters is returned as it is. Longer text keeps its first 1,000 characters, or 999 when the 1,000th is a high surrogate, so the text never ends in half a character, followed by ... (N more characters), where N counts the text's own characters left out. 1,000 is also the length above which the engine shortens the messages the class description lists, such as that of an InvalidExpressionException.

      Shorten first and escape after, escape(truncate(text)), so a cut never falls inside an escape and N counts the original text. Don't shorten text that is already escaped.

      Parameters:
      text - The text, not escaped
      Returns:
      The text, shortened if it was longer
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if text is null

    • quote

      public static String quote(String name)
      Shortens a name for a message to at most 200 characters (UTF-16 units), as truncate(java.lang.String) shortens text, with the same note after it, then escapes it. It adds no quotes: write them around it, as in "fact '" + MessageText.quote(name) + "'".
      Parameters:
      name - The name, such as a fact's, an option's or a class's
      Returns:
      The name, shortened if it was longer, then escaped
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if name is null
